newsitem.title: USA: Florida Lt. Gov. says Miami budget needs cushion.
newsitem.headline: Florida Lt. Gov. says Miami budget needs cushion.

text.p: Florida Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay said Monday that Miami needs more certain revenues and a bigger cushion in the budget for the current fiscal year.

MacKay, who heads a state oversight board appointed to guide Miami's recovery, also said he was worried that Congress may not authorize about $7 million of federal police grants that the city is counting on to balance its budget.
"I'm a little nervous about that," said MacKay. "I was in the Congress for a while. Some funny things happen."
However, MacKay said, "I believe they're 90 percent of the way there."
The oversight committee met for the first time Monday to review the deficit recovery plan that city commissioners adopted on Dec 30.
MacKay said the city had met the board's criteria that at least 60 percent of the $68 million deficit for fiscal 1997 must be covered by recurring revenues.
"I think the recurring revenues are pretty solid," MacKay told Reuters after the meeting.
But he said the $275 million budget, which has only $100,000 of nonallocated money, needed a bigger reserve.

"My concern was that there was no cushion there," MacKay said. "Yes, they did exactly what we required of them (adopt a balanced budget) but $100,000 in a $275 million budget, that's not much of a cushion. I suggested 10 percent."
City Manager Ed Marquez said the city may be able to meet that level if it counts property lease revenues that had not previously been included in the budget.
However, MacKay said, others on the five-member oversight board were less happy with the city's efforts.
"There were some hawkish comments. There's obviously some frustration with the failure to deal with the revenues," MacKay said.
The budget relies on employee concessions, new fees and federal grants, adding $21 million in new revenues, but continues to subsidize garbage services with general fund revenues.

The oversight board has until Jan 20 to accept or reject Miami's budget for fiscal 1997, which ends Sept 30. Gov. Lawton Chiles declared a fiscal emergency and appointed the board in December. The deficit had come to light several months earlier after three top city officials resigned to face federal corruption charges.

The oversight board was scheduled to meet again Tuesday to review a plan for the Miami Sports & Exhibition Authority to give Miami a one-time cash infusion of $12.6 million. The city could only spend the money on sports and tourism-related costs, but could use it to free up other money in its general fund.
